source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-239767:One block tall pointed dripstone generates excessively
source_meta._title: Clusters of dripstone (stalagmites) tend to generate abnormally frequent with thickness "tip" on tall caves

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition singleplayer world created and explored entirely in 1.18 Pre-release 4; world type set to Single Biome with the Dripstone Caves biome; commands enabled; player switched to Spectator mode for underground exploration.
preconditions: Install or configure a Minecraft Launcher installation for the exact affected version Minecraft: Java Edition 1.18 Pre-release 4. Do not use 1.18 Pre-release 5 or a later version for this reproduction.
Create a new world in the affected version rather than opening terrain generated by another Minecraft version.
Commands must be enabled so the player can execute the Spectator-mode command.
No world seed or target coordinates are supplied by the report; the cave search therefore takes place in a newly generated random world.
Keep the target terrain naturally generated and unmodified. Do not place, break, or replace pointed dripstone in the cave being inspected.

steps.action: Launch the Minecraft Launcher installation configured for Minecraft: Java Edition 1.18 Pre-release 4 and wait for the main menu to appear.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left portion of the Minecraft main menu identifies the running version as 1.18 Pre-release 4.

steps.action: From the main menu, select Singleplayer, then select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open.

steps.action: Set Game Mode to Creative. Creative is used only as a convenient starting mode before switching to the report-required Spectator mode.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Game Mode: Creative.

steps.action: Open More World Options and set Allow Cheats to ON so that the in-game gamemode command can be executed.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Allow Cheats: ON.

steps.action: Repeatedly select the World Type button until its value is Single Biome. Selecting Single Biome should make a Customize button available. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AMenu_screen/Java_Edition?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: World Type reads Single Biome and the Customize button is visible.

steps.action: Select Customize to open the biome-selection screen.
steps.success_cue: A screen containing a selectable list of biomes is open.

steps.action: Find and select Dripstone Caves in the biome list. Be careful to select the cave biome named Dripstone Caves rather than a similarly named block or world preset.
steps.success_cue: Dripstone Caves is highlighted as the selected biome.

steps.action: Select Done to confirm the Dripstone Caves biome and return to the world-creation options.
steps.success_cue: The biome-selection screen closes and the new-world configuration remains set to Single Biome.

steps.action: Because the report supplies no seed, leave the seed field empty, then select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: World generation begins and the player eventually appears in the newly created world.

steps.action: Do not begin exploring immediately. Wait until nearby terrain has rendered, the loading overlay is gone, and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The surface around the player is rendered and movement responds without initial world-loading pauses.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Type the Spectator-mode command exactly as supplied in exact_input, including the leading slash, and press Enter. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Wiki%3AProjects/Indonesian_translation/Mode_Penonton?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds and the player is switched to Spectator mode.

steps.action: Confirm Spectator movement by briefly pressing Space to fly upward and Left Shift, the default descend control, to fly downward. Release both controls after confirming vertical movement.
steps.success_cue: The player remains airborne and can move vertically without standing on a block.

steps.action: Aim the camera downward and hold the descend control, Left Shift by default, to pass through the surface and enter the underground. Use W to move forward, the mouse to steer, and Space if ascent is needed.
steps.success_cue: The player is below the surface and can pass through solid terrain while searching for open cave spaces.

steps.action: Explore horizontally through underground terrain in Spectator mode. Continue into previously unexplored areas rather than circling only beneath the spawn point. Pause whenever new terrain is rendering so chunk generation can finish before proceeding.
steps.success_cue: New underground terrain renders around the player and movement becomes responsive after each loading pause.

steps.action: Continue the search until a big or tall noise cave is revealed. For this reproduction, identify the target as a broad, naturally generated open cavern with a floor and ceiling separated by a clearly substantial vertical distance; do not use a narrow tunnel, a small enclosed cave, or a player-made excavation. If only small caves are found, continue exploring new terrain in the same world.
steps.success_cue: A broad, vertically tall natural cave is visible, with enough open space to view a sizeable portion of its floor.

steps.action: Move into viewing range of an unexplored or newly rendered section of that large cave until the floor, ceiling, and naturally generated dripstone features have finished generating and rendering. Do not alter any blocks.
steps.success_cue: The selected large-cave section is fully rendered, naturally generated floor stalagmite clusters are visible, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Release all movement controls and position the camera so that several naturally generated stalagmite clusters across the cave floor can be inspected together. Include as much of the cave's vertical space and ceiling as practical, but do not require the absence of stalactites above the clusters.
steps.success_cue: The camera is stationary and frames multiple natural stalagmite clusters on the floor of the loaded large/tall cave.

stor.handoff_condition: A newly explored section of a naturally generated large/tall noise cave in the Single Biome Dripstone Caves world has just finished loading. The player is stationary in Spectator mode, the terrain remains unmodified, and the camera is positioned to inspect multiple floor stalagmite clusters. Hand control to the observation subsystem now.
uncertainties: The report provides no deterministic seed, coordinates, or cave location, so the amount and direction of exploration cannot be predetermined.

The report does not define a numerical minimum height or volume for a 'big' or 'tall' noise cave. The plan therefore uses a broad open cavern with clearly substantial floor-to-ceiling separation and rejects small caves and narrow tunnels.

The report describes the generation pattern as frequent rather than universal. More than one large cave may need to be loaded and presented to the observation subsystem, but each candidate should be inspected after a single normal loading pass rather than modifying the terrain or repeatedly forcing chunk reloads.

The reporter speculates that affected floor clusters may lack stalactites above them within a noticeable range, but explicitly states that this may be wrong. Absence of overhead stalactites is therefore not treated as a reproduction precondition.
The report offers surface inspection as an alternative route, but this plan uses the primary large-noise-cave route because it most directly matches the stated setup and title.
